entry.translit: ṣāp̄ōh haṣ-ṣāp̄îṯ; ham-mᵉṣappeh; miṣpeh; mišmartî; šōmēr
entry.strongs: H6822 (ṣāp̄āh 'look out, keep watch'; Piel participle mᵉṣappeh); H6844 (ṣāp̄îṯ); H4707 (miṣpeh); H4931 (mišmeret); H8104 (šāmar; Qal participle šōmēr). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: the watch vocabulary of Isaiah 21 (roots ṣph and šmr)
entry.partOfSpeech: Piel participle used as noun; nouns; Qal participle used as noun; infinitive absolute + hapax noun
entry.literal: one who looks out; a look-out place; my place of guarding; one who guards; to watch the watch(?)
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: watchman (21:6) … watch-tower … my ward (21:8) … Watchman (21:11-12); set the watch (21:5). JPS 1917: a watchman; the watch-tower; my ward; Watchman; light the lamps (21:5). NJPS: a sentry; my Lord's lookout; my post; Watchman; 'Let the watchman watch!' (21:5). NRSV (not verified): sentinel; watchtower; my post; Sentinel; spread the rugs (21:5).
entry.wohChoice: 21:6 ham-mᵉṣappeh 'the lookout'; 21:8 miṣpeh 'the watchtower' and mišmartî 'my post'; 21:11-12 šōmēr 'Watchman' / 'The watchman' (wave ruling 6); 21:5 ṣāp̄ōh haṣ-ṣāp̄îṯ 'they set the watch' (ASV), the hapax ṣāp̄îṯ kept in its watch sense, with the 'rugs' and 'lamps' readings in commentary.
entry.rationale: Isaiah 21 uses two different nouns for the figure who watches. ham-mᵉṣappeh (21:6), a Piel participle of ṣph 'look out, keep watch' (BDB), is the one posted to see and report ('let him declare what he sees'). šōmēr (21:11-12), the participle of šmr 'guard, keep', is the guard asked about the night. ASV and JPS 1917 give 'watchman' for both and so hide the change of word. Wave ruling 6 asks for a consistent watch vocabulary within the chapter, and the line now keeps one English word per Hebrew noun: 'lookout' for mᵉṣappeh (NJPS 'sentry' and NRSV 'sentinel' show that the modern versions also separate it) and the ruled 'Watchman' for šōmēr. The places follow the standard renderings, miṣpeh 'watchtower' (ASV, JPS 1917) and mišmeret 'post' (NJPS; ASV 'ward'). 'Watchtower' shares an English stem with 'watchman' although the roots differ, and this is accepted because 'lookout tower' would be unidiomatic and NJPS's bare 'lookout' would be confused with the person. At 21:5 the hapax ṣāp̄îṯ is uncertain: ASV and NJPS take it as watch or watchman, JPS 1917 as lamps, and several lexicons and NRSV as rugs. The line keeps ASV and the commentary reports the alternatives, so nothing in the line depends on the root link. The entry is scoped to this chapter. Later Isaiah sites with the Qal participle ṣōp̄eh (52:8; 56:10) and šōmᵉrîm (62:6) are left to their Editors, who should keep or explicitly drop the same distinction. The choices are standard and carry no lens.

entry.strongs: H898 (bāḡaḏ 'act treacherously'); H7703 (šāḏaḏ 'devastate, destroy'). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.literal: the one dealing treacherously deals treacherously, and the one devastating devastates
entry.standardEnglish: the treacherous man dealeth treacherously, and the destroyer destroyeth (ASV); The treacherous dealer dealeth treacherously, and the spoiler spoileth (JPS 1917); The betrayer is betraying, The ravager ravaging (NJPS)
entry.wohChoice: 'the treacherous one deals treacherously, and the destroyer destroys' at 21:2: the bgd family 'treacherous … deal treacherously' of the stable 24:16, in the present tense because both members are participles; šôḏēḏ 'the destroyer' as in the chapter-16 draft at 16:4.
entry.rationale: The bgd paronomasia recurs in Isaiah at 21:2, 24:16 and 33:1, and a reader should be able to recognise it across chapters. The stable 24:16 renders the finite forms 'The treacherous have dealt treacherously; in treachery the treacherous have dealt treacherously' (overlay razi-li-pining-secret-crux-isaiah-24), so this entry fixes the same English family, 'treacherous / deal treacherously', for 21:2, with the tense following the Hebrew form: participle plus participle gives the present. ASV and JPS 1917 use the same family, so the choice is the PD baseline and not a new reading. NJPS's 'betrayer is betraying' was considered and rejected because it would break the concordance with 24:16. The NJPS note reports an emendation to passives ('betrayed … ravaged'), comparing 33:1. MT is kept under mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah. šôḏēḏ is 'the destroyer' (ASV), as the chapter-16 draft prints at 16:4 (mippᵉnê šôḏēḏ 'from the face of the destroyer'). JPS 1917 'spoiler' and NJPS 'ravager' are in commentary. When 33:1 is drafted its Editor should extend this entry. ISA-24:16 is not added to appliesTo here, because that stable chapter is outside this Editor's remit. The orchestrator may add it at merge with no change to the line.

entry.translit: midbar-yām; ban-negeḇ; ʿêlām; māḏay; bāḇel; dûmāh; śēʿîr; baʿrāḇ; dᵉḏānîm; têmāʾ; qēḏār
entry.strongs: H4057 + H3220 (midbār, yām); H5045 (negeḇ); H5867 (ʿêlām); H4074 (māḏay); H894 (bāḇel); H1746 (dûmāh); H8165 (śēʿîr); H6152 (ʿărāḇ); H1720 (dᵉḏānîm); H8485 (têmāʾ); H6938 (qēḏār). Strong's numbers from model recall, not concordance-verified.
entry.lemma: proper names and region names of Isaiah 21
entry.partOfSpeech: proper nouns; common nouns used as region names
entry.literal: wilderness of sea; in the south (dry land); Elam; Media / the Medes; Babylon; Dumah ('silence'); Seir; in Arabia / in the steppe; Dedanites; Tema; Kedar
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: the wilderness of the sea; in the South; O Elam; O Media; Babylon; Dumah; Seir; upon Arabia; Dedanites; Tema; Kedar. NJPS: 'Desert of the Sea'; the Negeb; Elam; Media; Babylon; 'Dumah'; Seir; 'In the Steppe'; Dedanites; Tema; Kedar.
entry.wohChoice: 'the wilderness of the sea' (21:1, wave ruling 6) with no region named in the line; bannegeḇ 'in the South' (ASV, JPS 1917; 'the Negeb' in commentary); 'O Elam … O Media' (21:2); 'Babylon' (21:9, ruling 4); 'Dumah' and 'Seir' (21:11, ruling 6); 'Arabia' for both baʿrāḇ (21:13; 'the steppe' in commentary); 'Dedanites', 'Tema', 'Kedar', 'the children of Kedar' (ASV spellings, ruling 4).
entry.rationale: Isaiah 21 is a sequence of short oracles headed by cryptic catchwords, and the names are where a translation is most tempted to explain. The line keeps the names as the Hebrew gives them. Identifications stay in commentary: the Sea-Land of southern Mesopotamia for midbar-yām (Wildberger, Isaiah 13-27; Blenkinsopp, Isaiah 1-39; recalled, not verified), the Ishmaelite Dumah of Gen 25:14 (NJPS note), Edom for Seir, and the north-Arabian oases and tribes for Tema, Dedan and Kedar. māḏay is 'Media' here and 'the Medes' at the stable 13:17. The two sites differ in syntax and the renderings are consistent with that. At 13:17 the name is the object of mēʿîr and governs plural verbs (yaḥšōḇû, yaḥpᵉṣû), so it is the people. At 21:2 it is a vocative beside the country name Elam, where ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS all print 'Media'. The rule is recorded here so that later sites follow it: 'the Medes' with plural agreement, 'Media' as the land or the vocative of a land. bannegeḇ is kept as 'in the South' (ASV, JPS 1917) because the article and the image of storms from the south fit the compass sense, and NJPS 'Negeb' is in commentary. baʿrāḇ is 'Arabia' at both occurrences of 21:13, following ASV and JPS 1917. The steppe reading (NJPS) and the LXX evidence for bāʿereḇ 'in the evening' are reported in commentary. The possible wordplay on dûmāh 'silence' is likewise reported and not put in the line. All renderings are attested in the PD baseline and carry no lens.

entry.partOfSpeech: nouns, verbs, participles, infinitives absolute, construct phrases
entry.literal: a hard vision; all its/her sighing; I am bent from hearing; my heart has wandered; he has set for me; to arrange … to eat, to drink; chariotry/riders; a pair of horsemen; he will attend with attention, much attention; Lord/my lord; all the nights; a troop of men; he shattered; my threshed one and son of my threshing floor; turn, come; in the scrub/forest; bring!/they brought; with his bread; the heaviness of war; number of bow, mighty ones of
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: grievous vision; all the sighing thereof; I am pained so that I cannot hear; My heart fluttereth; hath been turned; They prepare the table … they eat, they drink; a troop; horsemen in pairs; he shall hearken diligently with much heed; O Lord; whole nights; a troop of men; are broken; O thou my threshing, and the grain of my floor; turn ye, come; In the forest; they brought water; with their bread; the grievousness of war; the number of the archers, the mighty men.
entry.wohChoice: 21:2 'A harsh vision' (NJPS; departs from ASV 'grievous'); 'All its sighing I have brought to an end' (ASV). 21:3 'I am bowed down so that I cannot hear' (ʿwh 'be bent'; JPS 1917 'bent'; departs from ASV 'pained'), min privative. 21:4 'My heart reels' (tʿh 'stagger'; departs from ASV 'fluttereth'); śām rendered passive, 'has been turned' (ASV, JPS 1917). 21:5 the infinitives absolute descriptive, 'They prepare the table …' (ASV). 21:7, 9 reḵeḇ 'a troop'; ṣemeḏ pārāšîm 'horsemen in pairs'; 'he shall listen diligently, with great attention'. 21:8 'O Lord' (MT pointing); kol-hallêlôṯ 'whole nights' (ASV). 21:9 reḵeḇ ʾîš 'a troop of men' (wave ruling 13); šibbar passive 'are broken'. 21:10 'O my threshing, and the grain of my threshing floor' (ASV). 21:12 'turn back, come'. 21:13 bayyaʿar 'In the thicket' (JPS 1917 'thickets'; departs from ASV 'forest'; yaʿar stays 'forest' elsewhere in Isaiah). 21:14 hêṯāyû 'they brought' (ASV; the imperative of JPS 1917 and NJPS in commentary; PENDING FOUNDER RULING, staged alternative line: 'To meet the thirsty bring water! The inhabitants of the land of Tema met the fugitive with his bread.'); bᵉlaḥmô 'with his bread' (JPS 1917; departs from ASV 'their'). 21:15 kōḇeḏ 'the grievousness of war' (ASV). 21:17 'the number of the archers, the mighty men of the children of Kedar' (ASV; wave ruling 13).
entry.rationale: Each item is a single-site decision between ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS, made on lexical or grammatical grounds, with the alternatives recorded in commentary. None carries a project reading. (1) Five departures from ASV restore the lexical sense of the Hebrew, each attested in a PD or modern Jewish version. At 21:2 qāšeh is 'hard, harsh' (BDB; NJPS 'harsh'), which also leaves 'grievous' for kōḇeḏ at 21:15. At 21:3 the Niphal of ʿwh is 'be bent, bowed' (JPS 1917 'bent'), not 'pained'. At 21:4 tʿh is 'wander, stagger' (28:7), and 'reels' keeps the image that ASV 'fluttereth' loses. At 21:13 yaʿar covers scrub and thicket (BDB), which the Arabian steppe requires (JPS 1917 'thickets', NJPS 'scrub'), while 'forest' remains the rendering for wooded sites such as 10:18 and 10:34. At 21:14 the suffix of bᵉlaḥmô is singular (JPS 1917 'with his bread'). (2) Where the Hebrew is ambiguous the ASV construal is kept, and the alternative is put in commentary. At 21:4 and 21:9 the active verbs śām and šibbar have no expressed subject, and the English passive is the standard rendering of such an indefinite subject (NJPS supplies 'He' at 21:4). At 21:5 the infinitives absolute may be description (ASV, JPS 1917) or quoted orders (NJPS). At 21:8 the vocative ʾăḏōnāy follows the MT pointing, and NJPS's alternative 'my lord' is reported. At 21:14 hêṯāyû may be imperative (JPS 1917, NJPS) or perfect (ASV); the perfect is kept because the following qiddᵉmû is pointed as a perfect and the accents make the inhabitants of Tema its subject. The strongest evidence against this choice is Jer 12:9, where the identical form hêṯāyû follows the imperatives lᵉḵû ʾispû and is itself an imperative (WLC, checked by the Reviewer and the Editor). The perfect/imperative choice is therefore escalated. (3) Under wave ruling 13, ʾîš at 21:9 (a troop of riders) and gibbôrê at 21:17 name specific groups of warriors and keep 'men', as at the stable 13:3. The gender-neutral adam-humankind-ish-man-isaiah is not applied. (4) The kbd root of kōḇeḏ (21:15) is not governed by the strict kāḇôḏ 'glory' concordance of wave ruling 2, which covers the noun kāḇôḏ (21:16) only.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-4 (Isa 21): 'The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea' (21:1), 'The oracle concerning Dumah' (21:11) and 'The oracle concerning Arabia' (21:13). At 21:13 the heading has the preposition bᵉ- (maśśāʾ baʿrāḇ; ASV and JPS 1917 'upon Arabia'), and 'concerning' is kept so that the series of headings stays uniform. The bᵉ- form is noted in commentary.

Wave I-4 (Isa 21): the Translator's descriptive title 'Isaiah 21 — The oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea: the watchman, fallen Babylon, Dumah and Arabia' is kept. 'YHWH' is used at 21:10 and 21:17. Quotation marks follow the speeches: the divine charge 21:6-7, the lookout's report 21:8-9, the Seir call and the watchman's reply 21:11-12, and the oracle on Kedar 21:16-17.

Wave I-4 extension: 'the Lord' for standalone ʾăḏōnāy at 21:6 and 21:16, and the vocative 'O Lord' at 21:8, following the MT pointing (ASV, JPS 1917). NJPS's construct 'my Lord's lookout' and its marginal alternative 'my lord' (the lookout addressing the prophet, ʾăḏōnî) are reported in commentary.
Wave I-4 extension: 'YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel' at 21:10.
Wave I-4 extension: 'the God of Israel' at 21:10 and 21:17.
Wave I-4 extension: lower-case 'her gods' for ʾĕlōhêhā at 21:9 ('the carved images of her gods'), the gods of Babylon whose images are broken.

Wave I-4 (Isa 21): MT is kept, and the variants and emendations are reported in commentary. 21:1: the NJPS-noted emendation 'From the Desert'; LXX lacks 'of the sea' (Brenton's English). 21:2: the NJPS-noted emendations to the passives 'betrayed … ravaged' and to 'her merrymaking'. 21:5: the NJPS-noted emendation 'grasp' for mišḥû. 21:8: 1QIsaᵃ 'the watcher' for MT ʾaryēh 'a lion', reported in the NJPS note, which gives only the English. The Hebrew form (presumably hārōʾeh) is the Editor's reconstruction, and the reading was not checked against the scroll. 21:16: 1QIsaᵃ is reported to read 'three years' (not verified). Orchestrator: add '21:8 the watcher' and '21:16' to the variant list in wohChoice on merge; the Editor does not rewrite the field, to avoid a conflict with the parallel Editors.

Wave I-4 (ruling 14): kišnê śāḵîr at 21:16 is 'as the years of a hireling', the same wording as 16:14. ASV and JPS 1917 have 'according to the years of a hireling' and NJPS 'fixed like the years of a hired laborer'. MT bᵉʿôḏ šānāh 'Within a year' is kept against the reported 1QIsaᵃ 'three years'.
